text:
The evidence can't confirm that agricultural clearing caused the loss, because none of the tools identify a cause or what the land became afterward.

What the data shows:
- Hansen data flags 13.5 ha of tree-cover loss in 2025, or 3.9% of the 345.6 ha asset.
- JRC maps 98% of that area as forest in 2020.
- The MGAP 2021 map classes 13.1 ha as native forest and none as planted forest. So this is not a plantation harvest cycle.

Limits:
- No later year has been observed, so the loss doesn't meet the corroboration rule. I can't tell whether the land stayed cleared or regrew.
- No land-use data after the loss was provided, so I can't say whether crops or pasture followed.
- Other causes, such as fire, storm damage or selective logging, can't be excluded.

To test the agriculture hypothesis, check 2026 data when available, or review recent high-resolution imagery or field information.
